blocks.text: Expedia TAAP is Expedia Group’s booking platform for travel advisors: 200,000+ advisors at 38,000+ agencies across 85+ markets, in a business that passed $3 billion in bookings in 2025.

The Trips page was still the consumer “My Trips” list, with no traveler names, no search, and no filters. I led design across three generations, from 2023 to 2026, to turn it into a professional advisor workspace, working with Product, Engineering, Research, and Content.
The Gen 2 three-panel view decreased call volume to the customer center by 10%, and support tickets fell. Gen 3 is in progress.

items: Led design across all three generations
Mapped the live experience as a user flow and annotated every friction point
Ran qualitative user testing, surveys, and questionnaires with Research
Delivered specs, tokenized styles, and accessibility annotations at every handoff

items.label: fewer calls to the customer center after the 3-panel redesign

blocks.text: The original My Trips page was built for consumers. Advisors manage hundreds of client bookings at once and need to find one quickly, but the page gave them two tabs and a flat list of links.

image.alt: Original My Trips page with a flat list of hyperlinks

items: Two tabs only: Upcoming and Past and Canceled
Flat list of links: destination, date, itinerary number
No traveler name
No search, filters, or booking type indicators
No earnings, refund status, or advisor actions

blocks.text: The goal: a professional tool that helps advisors find a booking fast, see its status at a glance, and act on it.

gen1.title: From consumer list to data table

blocks.text: I replaced the consumer pattern with a professional data table and renamed “My Trips” to “Trips,” reframing the page as an advisor workspace.

items: Four status tabs
Sortable columns
Line-of-business icons showing booking type
Paginated results
Universal search with typeahead and full search states

image.alt: Generation 1 Trips page redesigned as a sortable data table

blocks.text: Gen 1 shipped and set the B2B table foundation. Research on it, plus a change in product direction, led to Gen 2.
Post-launch research and a product direction change called for a full redesign. Before designing, I mapped the live experience as a detailed user flow and annotated every friction point.
The Outlook-style, three-column layout gave advisors:

items: A persistent list on the left
Contextual actions in the center
An itinerary preview on the right

image.alt: Generation 2 three-panel Trips layout on desktop with the mobile list overlapping

blocks.text: Annotated specs, tokenized styles, and component documentation, with accessibility annotations, for desktop and mobile.

image.alt: Annotated Figma handoff of the three-panel Trips desktop and mobile screens

blocks.text: Qualitative user testing, surveys, and feedback questionnaires, run with the Research team, surfaced specific refinements. I organized 20+ changes into four categories for engineering prioritization.

items: A status sidebar with booking counts
Search by traveler name, with all agency bookings on request
Earnings, cancel waiver status, and share, modify, and export actions in the detail panel
Consumer pattern, professional need: advisors manage hundreds of bookings, so I replaced a flat list with a data table, then a three-panel workspace.
Change in direction: Gen 1 shipped, then a product shift called for a full redesign, so I mapped the live flow and annotated every friction point first.
Accessibility at scale: accessibility annotations at every handoff, for desktop and mobile.

image.alt: Generation 3 Trips dashboard after post-launch refinements
